correctness.rationale: For each color in a row, the local majority gives twice its row multiplicity at least selected row total minus one. Three row colors force exactly three singletons and paired mates in the other row, hence never more than three global colors. Otherwise each row has at most two colors, bounding the maximum by four. At four colors the palettes are disjoint, and summing the two inequalities in each row forces balanced color multiplicities and no simultaneous selected matched column; the converse is immediate. Small n=2,3 are addressed explicitly. Counting unordered equipartitions and disjoint column supports yields the exact sum and generating function. Independent reconstructed-graph finite verifier enumerated all unlabeled partial partitions up to n=5 and found exact values/counts; not misrepresented as proof of infinite range.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The primary paper has general upper bounds and exact families but its rectangular grids are products of paths, unlike two rows that are complete cliques. The complete multipartite formulas cannot be specialized to R_n, since R_n is not complete multipartite for n>=3. Its general bounds do not force a plateau at four or enumerate optimal partitions.

value.rationale: This exact invariant is a natural local-majority robustness problem recently introduced for arbitrary graph families. The matched-clique/line-graph family is a canonical highly dense product showing a sharp bounded four-color plateau despite linearly growing order and degree. More than an extremal number, the theorem classifies all optima via even disjoint support and provides a nontrivial factorial sum and EGF. These fine constraints are not a routine renaming of a prior complete-multipartite or path-grid result.
